extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent office examiners, judges, and law students
extracted.subtask_description: Legal principles governing the grant, amendment, repeal, construction, transfer (assignment/license), and extension of letters-patent, and the roles and powers of the Patent Office, its officers, and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent privilege created and defined by the grant of letters-patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of government conferring exclusive public use on an inventor is the grant of letters-patent; by them the scope, character, and duration of the inventor's exclusive right (monopoly) are specifically defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters-patent are both the measure and evidence of the monopoly; they conclusively determine the scope of the invention and the line between public use and the inventor's exclusive rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in description of the invention in letters-patent
rubrics_metrics.description: It is most important that the invention be accurately pointed out in the letters-patent so that the inventor's rights are permanently established within precise limits required by the nature of the discovery and its position in the arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Office exists to secure this accuracy by examining novelty and utility, correcting language, and resolving rival claims; errors in description can produce serious injustice if not corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office authority to amend defective letters-patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The law authorizes correction of errors in letters-patent even after issue, when errors occurred without the patentee's own misconduct or neglect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors may be of excess (granting more than invented) or omission (limiting right more than invention warrants); amendments are generally granted where error was not due to patentee's misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of illegal letters-patent by the courts, not the Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The power to repeal patents when the grant was improperly conferred is exercised by the courts of the United States; questions of repeal fall within judicial jurisdiction and are regulated by statute and general law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Congress may provide methods, repeal proceedings are not within the Patent Office's control; repeal rests on fundamental sovereign principles rather than mere administrative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters-patent interpreted by the courts as contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent creates a contract relation between the inventor and the public; the character and scope of rights and duties are expressed in the letters-patent and depend on judicial construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial construction governs the monopoly actually secured, regardless of the inventor's real intention or the Patent Office's attempted limits; rules for construing contracts apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights created by letters-patent are transferable
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to exclusive use conferred by letters-patent is a right collateral to the right to the invention itself and may be transferred in whole or in subdivisions for periods and on conditions the inventor desires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveyances are limited by judicial interpretation of the patent, and titles of claimants relate back to the original letters-patent as the source of their rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of letters-patent governed by statute and Patent Office rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings relating to grant are regulated partly by acts of Congress and partly by Patent Office rules; the Commissioner may adopt regulations for conduct of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules are subordinate to statutes and are binding like acts of Congress unless inconsistent; officers, parties, and attorneys must follow them until duly repealed, and departures are permitted only in necessary cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory prerequisites for a valid grant must be fulfilled
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain preliminary steps and conditions named in statute are essential to the grant; if statutory prerequisites are not fulfilled the letters-patent are null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Office has no power to dispense with these prerequisites; the issue of a patent is prima facie evidence that prerequisites existed, though for some prerequisites Patent Office decisions may be final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office rules and changes apply prospectively unless injustice results
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in Patent Office regulations may be made by authority that enacted them and after change the new rule must be obeyed even in pending cases unless injustice will thereby be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where new rules do not prejudice parties in pending cases they will be followed; courts' decisions operate retrospectively from the time rendered, while office rules apply to later-filed cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner, Acting Commissioner, and examiners: scope and limits of authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner has both judicial and ministerial powers; he is head of the Office and subject to Secretary supervision only where statutes do not control. The Acting Commissioner has the same legal effect; examiners are appointed to examine applications, correct descriptions, and determine novelty and utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner's ministerial powers over examination and granting are bounded by statutes and Office rules; examiners cannot decide matters already determined by superior tribunals, and the jurisdiction of tribunals does not change by person of incumbent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent solicitors and attorneys act under Office supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors may file and prosecute applications themselves but commonly use attorneys; such attorneys act under Commissioner supervision and may lose privileges for misconduct toward the Office or clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice is encouraged to facilitate Office work and secure patentees' rights; attorneys' obligations are governed by Office regulations and general law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent construction: first general rule — liberally construed in favor of inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are to be liberally construed in favor of the inventor so as to give appropriate effect to the invention as claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liberal construction permits interpretation in accordance with the real nature of the invention unless the patent's language clearly forbids such interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on liberal construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule of liberal construction does not authorize departure from the language of the letters-patent nor an equivocal or elastic interpretation of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will not stretch patent language beyond its words; liberal construction must still respect clear language and limits set by the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent construction: entire patent construed together as an indivisible instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: An entire patent — claims, specification, drawings — must be construed together; different parts may clarify and restrict claims but may not enlarge them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other portions of the patent may be used to restrict the claims to their proper scope but cannot be used to broaden them beyond the claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent construction: words and phrases interpreted in their ordinary sense if possible
rubrics_metrics.description: When construing letters-patent, words and phrases should, if possible, be given their ordinary meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical application includes looking to state of the art at date of invention and other acts or circumstances to show nature of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules of construction for particular claim-types
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules apply to pioneer patents, re-issued patents, patents granted by act of Congress, claims for combinations, improvements, claims for principles/functions/effects, claims to an indivisible entirety versus separate devices, use of foreign words, 'substantially as described', 'generic', and terms admitting degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These special rules modify general construction principles and address recurring interpretive issues; courts have developed specific doctrines for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents repealable in the interest of the public in specified classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings for repeal in the interest of the public rest on fundamental principles and occur in classes of cases such as patents obtained by fraud or where subject-matter cannot lawfully be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such proceedings are sometimes necessary and are instituted by bill in equity in the name of the United States; procedure and judgment are regulated by statute and equity practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers: two classes — transfer of invention and monopoly vs invention alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers of patented inventions are of two classes: first-class transfers convey both the invention and the monopoly (e.g., assignment/grant of entire interest); second-class transfers convey the invention but not the monopoly (e.g., certain licenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No transfer can be of the first class unless it conveys the entire interest or an undivided portion of the entire interest for the whole or a definite part of the United States; forms of transfer correspond to these classes (assignment/grant vs license).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment: form, effect, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment transfers property in a patented invention and is distinguished from grants and licenses; form and general requisites must be observed, and assignments transfer only the invention specifically assigned (and, for American patents, only the monopoly created by those patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments before patent, assignments of extensions, implied warranties of title, recording requirements (record constructive notice), and relation of legal/equitable titles are governed by detailed principles (see respective sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: License: defined and distinguished from assignment/grant
rubrics_metrics.description: A license is any transfer of less than the entire interest or an undivided part of the entire interest in a patented invention; the invention, not the monopoly, is transferred by a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licenses may be express or implied; express licenses can cover make/use/sell rights and be exclusive or non-exclusive; implied licenses arise in sale, permission to make before application, employer/employee contexts, estoppel, and are construed in specific ways (scope as to time, territory, method, quantity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied license principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Implied licenses can arise in favor of purchasers at lawful sales, from permission to make before patent application, in employer/employee and copartner relations, and by estoppel; their scope may be unlimited as to time/territory/method/quantity in some contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An implied license to use does not necessarily include the right to make or to sell for traffic; unknown prior agreements of licensor do not restrict an implied license in some sale contexts; estoppel-based licenses arise where conduct warrants it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of letters-patent: conditions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions exist by statute and practice; extensions must be for the same invention as the original, are not permitted for invalid patents, and are granted under conditions and procedures (some within Patent Office jurisdiction, some by Congress reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions of the Patent Office on extensions may be final; extensions affect rights of assignees and may be assigned under rules; special acts of Congress may provide for extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent is prima facie evidence of fulfillment of prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue of letters-patent is prima facie evidence that the statutory prerequisites for grant existed and were sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the patent is prima facie evidence, courts and the Patent Office can later inquire into sufficiency; for some prerequisites the Patent Office's decision is final, but courts may later reverse when proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings and jurisdictional presumption in Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings in the Patent Office are presumed regular; the Commissioner acts under Secretary oversight but judicial acts of the Commissioner (in classes authorized by law) are not appealable to the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ministerial and judicial acts of the Office are distinguished; the Acting Commissioner has full legal effect; examiners' duties are fixed and their decisions are reviewable in appropriate forums.
